clue.text: Knife literally raised in fight

indicators.note: in tells us the reversed piece sits inside the word for a fight

parts.note: a set-to is a brief fight or scrap

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the piece is read upwards, so backwards

explanation.surface: A knife is brandished, quite literally, during a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'literally' looks like an adverb on the surface but gives its standard abbreviation; 'raised' turns it upwards in this down clue, and 'in' sets that inside a set-to.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a short dagger with a slender tapering blade.

clue.text: Greater than governor over North Dakota

parts.note: a bey was a provincial governor in the Ottoman Empire
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over
ND is the postal abbreviation for the US state of North Dakota

explanation.surface: Someone outranks a state governor in North Dakota.
explanation.walkthrough: A bey was an Ottoman provincial governor; O is the cricket abbreviation for an over.
explanation.definitionFit: Beyond can mean exceeding or more than, as in beyond expectations.

clue.text: Heard successors give up

indicators.note: Heard says the answer is a word that sounds like the clue's synonym when spoken

parts.note: seed, in the biblical sense, means descendants or those who come after

explanation.surface: Heirs are told they must surrender something.
explanation.walkthrough: Seed in the old biblical sense means offspring, those who succeed you.
explanation.definitionFit: To cede territory or a right is to surrender or relinquish it.

clue.text: Magnificent piece of old Manx cat

indicators.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so this word for a cat loses its last letter

parts.note: puss is a familiar word for a cat

explanation.surface: A splendid artwork depicts an old tailless cat from the Isle of Man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manx' (the tailless cat breed from the Isle of Man) docks the end of PUSS to give PUS.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a musical or artistic work, the great one being a magnum opus.

clue.text: Everywhere stormy dawned fair

indicators.note: stormy suggests the letters of the following words are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: A tempestuous morning cleared to fine weather across the whole country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stormy' reshuffles DAWNED FAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Far and wide is an idiom meaning over a great area, in all places.

clue.text: Reared animals for stage

indicators.note: in a down clue reared means lifted upright, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: pets are animals kept at home

explanation.surface: Farm animals were raised to appear in a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reared' turns PETS upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is a stage in a process, as in the next step.

clue.text: Steals pants in America

definitions.meaning: to trouser money is British slang for pocketing it dishonestly

explanation.surface: Someone shoplifts underwear in the States.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain pants means underpants, so 'pants' misleads; the clue wants the American sense of outer legwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Trouser as a verb is British slang for pocketing, and US pants are the British outer legwear.

clue.text: Check artist's standing with the others

indicators.note: in a down clue standing means upright, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword staple for artist
the rest means the others or the remainder

explanation.surface: Someone verifies a painter's status relative to fellow artists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing' sets RA upright in this down clue, giving AR.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrest a process is to check or halt it.

clue.text: Subject of article about space

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the word for a space is read backwards

parts.note: an em is a printer's unit of space

explanation.surface: A news item concerns outer space.
explanation.walkthrough: An em is a typographical space; 'about' flips EM.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the topic or subject of a talk or piece of writing.

clue.text: Drunk Democrat leaves Republican tradesperson

indicators.note: leaves means the letter for Democrat goes and the letter for Republican takes its place

parts.note: plastered is slang for very drunk
D is the abbreviation for a US Democrat
R is the abbreviation for a US Republican

explanation.surface: An inebriated Democrat walks out on a Republican builder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' swaps the D at the end of PLASTERED for R.
explanation.definitionFit: A plasterer is a skilled worker who applies plaster to walls and ceilings.

clue.text: Lesson I arranged for Leo's mate

indicators.note: arranged says the letters of the words before it are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A lesson is set up for a friend named Leo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges LESSON I.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo is the lion of the zodiac, and a lion's mate is a female lion.

clue.text: A smuggler hides cut drug in small glass vessel

indicators.note: hides means the smuggler contains the shortened drug inside it

parts.note: a mule is someone who smuggles drugs across borders

indicators.note: cut means the word for drug loses its final letter

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A drug runner conceals adulterated narcotics in a little glass phial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' is drug-dealer slang for adulterating, but here it trims a letter; 'hides' then tucks the result inside the courier word.
explanation.definitionFit: An ampoule is a small sealed glass capsule holding a dose of medicine.

clue.text: American president's undergarment

definitions.meaning: The nickname of US president Theodore Roosevelt

explanation.walkthrough: The teddy bear was named after Theodore 'Teddy' Roosevelt.
explanation.definitionFit: Theodore Roosevelt was known as Teddy, and a teddy is a camisole-and-knickers lingerie piece.

clue.text: Sentimental endearment director expressed after end of play

indicators.note: after places the trimmed endearment behind the picked letter
end of picks the final letter of the word play
expressed in its sense of pressed out: the director's letter is squeezed out of the endearment

parts.note: ducky is a British term of endearment, like dear

explanation.surface: A director gushes a mushy pet name once the play is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expressed' is read as pressed out, so the director's letter is squeezed from the endearment; 'after' puts what remains behind the last letter of play.
explanation.definitionFit: Yucky is informal for mawkishly sentimental, as well as disgusting.

clue.text: Jam lover's one way of working with damsons originally

parts.note: MO is modus operandi, a way of working

indicators.note: originally means take the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A jam enthusiast's method for handling damsons.
explanation.walkthrough: The Jam were a 1970s-80s British band beloved of mods, the sharp-suited youth subculture, so jam here is the band, not the preserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A mod was a fan of bands like The Jam in the mod revival.

clue.text: Possibly aim to enter with Lady Penelope?

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters could be arranged in another way

explanation.surface: Someone hopes to arrive accompanied by an aristocratic lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges AIM TO ENTER. Lady Penelope is the aristocratic puppet agent in the British TV series Thunderbirds; the question mark marks her as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Penelope was a string puppet in Thunderbirds, so she is an example of one.

clue.text: Representative sample of collagen treatment

indicators.note: sample of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sales rep hands out a trial of a collagen skin product.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent acts on behalf of another person, as their representative.

clue.text: A way to welcome company in Berkshire town

indicators.note: to welcome means the word for way takes in the company abbreviation

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A method for greeting a firm visiting a county town.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot is a town in Berkshire, an English county west of London, famous for its racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot, home of Royal Ascot races, is a town in the county of Berkshire.

clue.text: Time Henry omitted beginning of the Lord's prayer

indicators.note: omitted says the letter for Henry is dropped from the time word

parts.note: an hour is a unit of time
H is the symbol for the henry, the SI unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A moment when Henry left out the opening of a prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'omitted' takes H from HOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lord's Prayer opens with the words Our Father.

clue.text: Local Iron Age construction's closer to hill

indicators.note: construction suggests the letters are built up into a new form
closer to means the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A prehistoric structure is the nearest thing to a hill fort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'construction' rebuilds IRON AGE as REGIONA, and 'closer to' adds the L of hill.
explanation.definitionFit: Regional and local both describe something limited to a particular area.

clue.text: Very ill person in short top and a cape

parts.note: cardi is short for cardigan, a knitted top
C is a map abbreviation for cape

explanation.surface: A sick patient wears a cropped top and a cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' is not a trimming here: cardi is an accepted short form of cardigan.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardiac as a noun is a person with heart disease, seriously unwell.

clue.text: Special soul music from Jamaica

parts.note: ka is the soul or spirit in ancient Egyptian belief

explanation.surface: A special kind of soul music comes from the Caribbean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soul music' tempts, but soul is KA, the ancient Egyptian spirit; The Specials were also a ska band.
explanation.definitionFit: Ska is a fast upbeat style of popular music that began in Jamaica.

clue.text: Attacked tired Welsh politician first

indicators.note: first places the politician's letters at the front, ahead of the word for tired

parts.note: AM was an Assembly Member of the Welsh Assembly
bushed is informal for exhausted

explanation.surface: A weary Welsh politician was the first to be set upon.
explanation.walkthrough: AM stood for Assembly Member of the Welsh Assembly, now the Senedd.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambushed means attacked by surprise from a hidden position.

clue.text: Loose goods stored in alcove

indicators.note: stored in means the goods letters are placed inside the alcove word

parts.note: a bay is a recess or alcove
G stands for good, so GG for goods in the plural

explanation.surface: Untied merchandise is kept in a recess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stored in' places the goods inside the alcove; G for good is standard, doubled for the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Baggy clothing hangs loosely and is not tight-fitting.

clue.text: Extremely cold drink

definitions.meaning: a British type of draught beer

explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is a well-hopped British ale served in pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A bitter wind is biting and freezing, and bitter is a kind of English beer.

clue.text: Single drink

definitions.meaning: a quick ... is an informal word for a drink, as in fancy ...?

explanation.definitionFit: One is a lone unit, and informally an alcoholic drink, as in one for the road.

clue.text: Heath Robinson checks pulse

indicators.note: checks in the sense of holds back, keeping the answer contained within the name

explanation.surface: The cartoonist Heath Robinson takes someone's pulse.
explanation.walkthrough: W. Heath Robinson was a British cartoonist famed for absurdly elaborate contraptions; 'checks' holds the answer within his name.
explanation.definitionFit: A throb is a strong regular beat, like a pulse.

clue.text: Melancholy way of the French footloose rich

parts.note: rue is French for street, a way

indicators.note: footloose read as loose its foot: the word for rich loses its bottom letter

parts.note: full means rich, as in a full flavour

explanation.surface: A gloomy French road suits the carefree wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'footloose' is read as losing its foot, the last letter in a down clue: FULL becomes FUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Rueful means regretful and sorrowful, close in sense to melancholy.

clue.text: New toot designed for sound of car horn?

indicators.note: designed suggests the letters are made over into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A newly designed hoot for a vehicle's horn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges NEW TOOT; the question mark flags the definition as one example, a horn sounding two notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-tone horn alternates between two notes, a typical sound of an emergency vehicle.

clue.text: State Cook discovered circumnavigating Hawaii

indicators.note: circumnavigating means going round, so the uncovered letters surround the state abbreviation
discovered in its sense of uncovered: the outer letters of the word are stripped away

parts.note: HI is the postal abbreviation for Hawaii

explanation.surface: Captain Cook found a state while sailing round Hawaii.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered' strips the cover from COOK, leaving OO, which goes 'circumnavigating' HI.
explanation.definitionFit: Ohio is one of the fifty states of the USA.

clue.text: Insanity of head pursuing deterrent theory

indicators.note: pursuing means the headland word follows behind the theory's letters

parts.note: MAD is mutually assured destruction, the nuclear deterrence doctrine
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness

explanation.surface: Madness lies in a leader chasing a nuclear-deterrence doctrine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' suggests a leader, but it means a headland; 'pursuing' puts that after the Cold War doctrine of mutually assured destruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Madness is a state of mental derangement, synonymous with insanity.

clue.text: Old Asian honeyed wine is mentioned

indicators.note: is mentioned says the answer is said like the word for the drink

parts.note: mead is a drink fermented from honey

explanation.surface: An ancient Asian's honey wine gets a mention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is mentioned' means the answer is spoken the same as MEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The Medes were an ancient Iranian people of Media in western Asia.

clue.text: A head of department initially returned capital

indicators.note: returned means the assembled letters are read back in the opposite direction
initially means the first letter of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: A departmental head came back to the capital first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes HOD from head of department; with A that gives AHOD, which 'returned' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Doha is the capital city of Qatar.

clue.text: Lean meat diced briefly in a stew with head of artichoke

indicators.note: in a stew suggests the letters are stirred up together like a stew
briefly means the word loses its last letter
head of means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A recipe: dice lean meat for a stew topped with artichoke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' docks DICED to DICE, 'head of' adds the A of artichoke, and 'in a stew' shuffles MEAT DICE A.
explanation.definitionFit: Emaciated means abnormally thin, gaunt, so lean in the extreme.

clue.text: Type of music for the audience

definitions.meaning: a style of electronic dance music
the ... is the audience in a theatre, as in a full ...

explanation.surface: A style of music aimed at the listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: House is an electronic dance genre, and a theatre's house is its audience.
